decisions.r0-4-precedence: R04-I2: the mode's own fallback-only step is run BEFORE a wrong-context report, even when another mode's row holds for the unit (Step 6 item 1 carve-out; KB 'How a session runs' says the same). apiContract.note: tests dictate this model surface; Unit loses `resumed`
apiContract.SessionOptions: { enabled: string[]; haltOn?: string; project?: ProjectFacts }
apiContract.ProjectFacts: { prd: 'template'|'populated'; techTemplates: number; initiatives: number; epics: number; stories: number }
apiContract.semantics: without `project` a session is story-scoped (rows 6-11 only); with it rows 1-5 apply: row1 prd template; row2 prd populated AND techTemplates>=3; row3 initiatives=0 AND epics=0; row4 initiatives>0 AND epics=0; row5 epics>0 AND stories=0. Rows are evaluated in cascade order 1..11 (first match wins across rows 1-5 and 6-11); a matching row whose step is disabled is skipped and evaluation continues at the next row. row 7 effect leaves the unit unchanged; the Step 6 hand-off (row 7 ran for the unit in this session -> row 8 step implement) is session state, never a Unit field. When the session ran no step because no enabled row OF THE MODE selects (whatever other modes' rows hold), and the mode lists a Fallback-only step that the profile enables and the backlog has NO EPICS (not merely no stories), that step is run once; a HALT it raises is surfaced as-is (exit 'halt', halted = the step). Only when it is not run does the wrong-context / all-disabled / nothing-to-do ending apply.
